sources.news_title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang allegedly an affair with a second employee
sources.text:
A third Jensen Huang affair just dropped
Jensen Huang, now sporting the title of "former" Nvidia CEO, wasn't just having an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Nor was he juggling two extramarital relationships — as another slightly less politically-charged claim surfaced on Wednesday, Nov., alleging he was romantically involved with Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, Kimberly Powell.
No, in the wake of Huang's Thursday resignation, a third allegation has surfaced that suggests Huang was intimately involved in at least one other company employee while married to wife and Nvidia fortune co-controller Lori Huang.
Two former Nvidia employees spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity for its Nov. 12 report, which did not name the employee. Nvidia declined to comment on the allegations, and none of the involved parties responded to Reuters' requests for comment.
You May Also Like
The internet has been on fire since the news dropped.
    
        This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.
    
Huang previously admitted to being unfaithful to his wife after reports linked him to Chinese businesswoman and cloud computing exec Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le. According to the New York Times, Alice Huang was being surveilled by U.S. counterintelligence authorities for suspected espionage. She is a controlling shareholder of Chinese computing company Megaspeed, which was previously investigated by U.S. authorities for allegedly skirting U.S. export controls to bring advanced chips to Chinese markets. Megaspeed is still listed as an official cloud partner of Nvidia, Reuters reported.
Nvidia, one of the most valuable tech companies in the world, saw its stock plummet after news broke of Huang's ties to the Megaspeed shareholder. In just four days, the company has lost $450 billion in market value.
President Donald Trump, who chose Huang as one of his tech advisors, has so far maintained his support of Huang while denying knowledge of the relationships. Following the CEO's resignation, Trump celebrated Huang's career — and then floated former Apple CEO Tim Cook as Huang's replacement.
Topics Nvidia

sources.news_title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Reportedly Had Affair With Second Employee
sources.text:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned today amid a scandal involving an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and an executive that reported to him. Now, it's been reported that Huang allegedly had an affair with a second employee.
Huang allegedly had an intimate relationship with a second employee, according to two sources inside Nvidia and reported by Reuters. However, Reuters hasn't named the second employee, and attempts to reach her were not successful.
This third revelation comes just hours after Huang resigned from Nvidia, following an internal investigation that kicked off on Sunday. Huang himself came out and admitted to one of the affairs in a letter sent to Nvidia staff and obtained by The BBC. Then, following a meeting where Nvidia's board weighed ousting Huang, the former CEO resigned.
In the meantime, Nvidia's board has named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while the company searches for a new leader. Nvidia is considering both internal and external applicants, but there has been talk that Apple Senior Vice President of Hardware Technlogy Johny Srouji is being considered for the role, according to MacRumors.
As for Huang itself, it's not clear where he's going to end up, or what he's going to do going forward. Last night, Elon Musk posted on X that it "would be an honor" to hire Huang... but it's doubtful that he'd end up at any of Musk's companies.
Either way, Huang has been leading Nvidia since 1993, and has seen the company grow from being a niche gaming hardware company to the backbone of the entire AI industry. His resignation is going to send shockwaves throughout the entire tech biz. One of the biggest casualties might end up being PC gaming altogether. After all, Nvidia makes up for a massive 73% of Steam's install base, according to the latest Steam Hardware survey, but the company still dropped gaming from its earnings reports earlier this year. And, now with Jensen's departure, it's unlikely that PC hardware is going to get the same level of support.

sources.news_title: How Did He Have Time to Work?
sources.text:
I’m sure you have seen the podcast clips where highly motivated CEOs talk about how they have the same 24 hours that you and I do — they’ve just figured out how to optimize them. Despite what they say, it seems like it would be pretty hard to run a multi-trillion dollar business, have a family, and still catch up on The Gilded Age every week. Now imagine doing that while also having multiple extramarital affairs. It sounds exhausting to me personally, but somehow Jensen Huang, the freshly ousted Nvidia CEO and married man of more than 40 years, made it work.
Nvidia was rocked earlier this week after Huang admitted to having an affair with a woman identified by the U.S. government as a Chinese spy. On Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang was having a second affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care and one of Huang’s direct reports. Sources told the paper that Huang and Powell were caught on video being “affectionate” at an Nvidia conference outside of San Jose in March.
After the revelation of his second affair, Huang resigned from Nvidia on Thursday. That was probably the wise move, considering he probably knew what was coming next. A few hours after his resignation, Reuters reported that Huang had a third affair, also with one of his Nvidia employees. The outlet did not name the woman.
Where did Huang find the time? This is a guy who once told Joe Rogan that he reads “several thousand emails a day.” Huang famously structured Nvidia so he had 60 people reporting to him directly instead of delegating that work out to the rest of his C-suite. He claimed to have a 14-hour workday. You’re telling me he also found time to build three romantic relationships outside his marriage? Maybe some people really do have more hours in the day.

sources.news_title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Had Relationship With Another Employee, Sources Say
sources.text:
Nov. 12 — Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with another company employee, according to two people familiar with the matter, adding another development to the personal controversy that preceded his departure from the artificial intelligence chipmaker.
The latest revelation follows reports of Huang’s relationships with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence suspects of having ties to Chinese espionage, and Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare.
Attempts to reach the woman were unsuccessful.
Nvidia declined to comment. Jensen Huang, Powell and a representative for Nvidia’s board did not respond to requests for comment. Alice Huang could not be reached.
The former CEO acknowledged having an affair in a November 8 statement following reports about his relationship with Alice Huang, although he did not identify her by name.
Resignation Follows Mounting Controversy
Huang, 63, is married and co-founded Nvidia, transforming it from a graphics chipmaker into one of the world’s most influential technology companies.
Pressure on him to leave intensified following reports about his relationship with Alice Huang and the allegations surrounding her connections to China.
The controversy also raised questions about Nvidia’s corporate governance, security procedures and the potential implications for U.S. national security.
Earlier this month, Nvidia’s board launched an investigation, led by independent directors and outside legal counsel, into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. At the time, the board publicly expressed confidence in him.
Huang ultimately stepped down on Thursday, bringing an abrupt end to his leadership of the company.
Nvidia appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement. The company is considering both internal and external candidates.
Nvidia’s Departure Could Affect the Wider AI Industry
Huang’s exit comes at a sensitive time for the artificial intelligence industry, where Nvidia occupies a central position as a supplier of advanced processors and computing infrastructure.
The company has used its substantial financial resources to support the broader AI ecosystem through complex investment and financing arrangements. These include backing cloud computing providers and AI laboratories, some of which also purchase Nvidia’s chips.
Those relationships have helped expand demand for the company’s hardware and accelerate the development of AI infrastructure.
However, Huang’s departure could raise questions about how Nvidia approaches these investments and partnerships under new leadership.
His influence extended beyond the company’s products. He played a significant role in shaping relationships with major customers, technology partners and governments, making the leadership transition particularly consequential.
Board Investigation and Leadership Search Continue
The latest report adds to the scrutiny surrounding Nvidia’s internal oversight as the company adjusts to life without its longtime chief executive.
The board’s investigation into whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation remains an important part of the controversy.
Meanwhile, Kress is responsible for maintaining operational stability while Nvidia identifies a permanent successor.
The company faces the challenge of reassuring investors, protecting its relationships across the AI industry and maintaining confidence in its long-term strategy.
Nvidia Shares Remain Under Pressure
Nvidia shares fell 5.5% on Thursday in active trading, extending a period of significant losses.
The stock has now shed more than 30% of its value since reaching its peak in early October.
The decline reflects a combination of concerns surrounding Huang’s departure, questions about corporate governance and uncertainty over the future direction of the AI industry.
For Nvidia, the immediate challenge is no longer simply managing a leadership transition. It must also address the broader questions raised by the controversy while preserving the business relationships and technological advantages that helped establish its dominance in artificial intelligence.

sources.text:
Just days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly admitted that he had cheated on his wife with a woman who the US government suspects of being a Chinese spy, the New York Times revealed that he had a second affair with Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell — which is strictly forbidden under Nvidia’s code of conduct.

And as investors continued to debate what matters more — his freewheeling love life or the possibility of having given up corporate secrets to the United States’ biggest adversary — Reuters now reports that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee.

Beyond the baffling extent of Huang’s extramarital affairs, the growing scandal could have significant implications on a geopolitical scale. A Department of Commerce investigation into her employer, a Singapore-based data center company, was abruptly shut down by the Department of Justice last year, leaving plenty of questions unanswered.

sources.news_title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO After Affairs: Live Updates
sources.text:
As investors have pumped trillions of dollars into artificial intelligence companies, chipmakers and data center developers, the economy has come to rely on the industry as its primary — some would argue only — reliable driver of growth.
No company has been more central to that growth than Nvidia, whose chips fill the data centers that power A.I. and whose money helps to finance them. And, at least until this week, it was impossible to imagine Nvidia without Jensen Huang, its high-flying, leather-clad co-founder and chief executive.
All of which means that Mr. Huang’s resignation on Thursday, following a made-for-Hollywood series of scandals, matters not just for the company and its investors, but for virtually every American.
Or, as Aaron Klein, an expert in financial regulation at the Brookings Institution, put it: “Can one C.E.O.’s sex life take down the economy?”
The answer, in a literal sense, is almost certainly no. No one believes that Mr. Huang’s resignation will, by itself, bring the A.I. boom to an end, let alone plunge the economy into a recession. Nvidia’s stock price tumbled on Thursday, but the broader market barely budged.
But Mr. Klein’s quip spoke to the unique role that Mr. Huang played at Nvidia, and that his company has played in the A.I. build out.
Nvidia controls about 90 percent of the market for the most advanced chips used to train and run A.I. models. The turmoil at the company could create an opening for competitors such as AMD and Intel to encroach on that market share. But there is little reason to think that Mr. Huang’s resignation will threaten Nvidia’s ability to develop and produce the chips it has promised its customers.
But Nvidia isn’t just the dominant chipmaker. It is also the “central bank of A.I.,” helping to finance the industry’s growth through a series of complex deals with its customers and suppliers.
When OpenAI signed a lease for a 10-gigawatt data center in Ohio in August, it was Nvidia that provided $105 billion in loan guarantees. Days later, the company teamed up with several Wall Street firms to create a $500 billion fund to help finance A.I.-related infrastructure. Nvidia owns a more than 10 percent stake in CoreWeave, a big data center operator, and has guaranteed billions of dollars in its loans.
Its loan commitments and financing arrangements would make Nvidia the 10th largest bank in the country, according to an estimate from Ryan Cummings, the chief of staff for the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research.
“Nvidia is at the center of this circular financing, and obviously at the center of Nvidia is Jensen Huang,” Mr. Cummings said. “He has been the driving force, pretty inarguably, behind a lot of the A.I. build-out.”
Without Mr. Huang in charge, Nvidia’s role could change, Mr. Cummings said. And while it is possible that other companies will step in to fill the gap, that isn’t guaranteed.
Mr. Huang’s departure comes at a delicate time for the A.I. industry. There have been signs in recent months that investors are growing more skeptical that companies will deliver returns that justify the huge investments they are making in A.I., or at least that those returns could take longer than expected to materialize.
And Democrats’ sweeping victories in last week’s midterm elections could lead to new restrictions on data center construction, which could jeopardize the industry’s boom.
“At a point when people are already on edge about this trade, it’s another piece of uncertainty,” Mr. Cummings said.
In the past, when confidence in the A.I. story has wavered, Mr. Huang and Nvidia have been the ones to calm doubts, reporting huge sales figures or stepping in to provide financing to data center projects whose future seemed in jeopardy. This time, it isn’t clear who will fill the void.
“Could the single largest A.I. company C.E.O.’s impropriety be the start of the pop of the bubble?” Mr. Klein asked. “Yes, as crazy as that sounds. Particularly when one company is so central.”
Bubbles are inherently unpredictable: It isn’t clear, ahead of time, what will flip the psychological switch that causes them to burst. The muted market reaction of financial markets to the news on Thursday suggests that investors aren’t losing faith in the A.I. trade.
But Mr. Klein said the Nvidia mess should be a warning that the complex web of A.I. financing arrangements is threatening financial stability.
“It looks like the financial regulators are sleeping through the alarm clock,” he said.
If Nvidia’s new leadership takes a more cautious approach to financing, that could have implications for the broader economy. The data center boom has helped to prop up the construction and manufacturing industries, at a time when tariffs, high interest rates and uncertainty have limited demand from other sectors.
Still, the breakneck pace of the A.I. build-out has also pushed up inflation and raised borrowing costs. Many economists argue that a modest slowdown would be healthy.
The more immediate risk, economists say, is that a loss of confidence in the A.I. story leads to a steep drop in the stock market. The strength of the market has helped prop up consumer spending even as wage growth has cooled.
If the A.I. trade unravels because of an abrupt curtailment in investment, “that is more recessionary,” said Pooja Sriram, an economist at Barclays. “That’s when there is a more material shakeout in the stock market that transcends to how consumers feel. Balance sheets are hit and that could escalate very quickly into a downturn.”
Colby Smith contributed reporting.
